quran.note: Ilyas asks his people why they call on Ba’l and leave the best of creators; they deny him, and he is left a favourable mention.
Ilyas is listed among the righteous.

scholarly.work: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (abridged English edition, read on Quran.com)
scholarly.author: Ibn Kathir
scholarly.summary: Explains “Ba’l” as lord. Quotes Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Qatadah and al-Suddi on the word. Ikrimah and Qatadah tie it to the Yemeni language, Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam says it was an idol at Baalbek, and al-Dahhak says it was an idol. He says “Ilyasin” is a dialect form of the name from Bani Asad. He names no king.

views.who: Ikrimah and Qatadah, as quoted by Ibn Kathir
views.work: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (abridged English edition, read on Quran.com), on 37:123
views.view: The word means “lord” in the language of Yemen.
